Unlike direct image-space optimization which traps gradient descent in local minima under domain shift, RISP enables optimization in a rendering-invariant state space [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that direct image-space optimization traps gradient descent in local minima under domain shift, while RISP enables optimization in a rendering-invariant state space. Source [S1] explicitly supports both parts of this claim: 1) It states that 'directly optimizing L defined on the image space rarely works when the two rendering domains are vastly different' and that 'local optimization techniques like gradient-descent can be trapped into local minima easily if {Ii} and {Iref_i} are not close enough.' 2) It introduces RISP to 'redefine L in a state-like space' where the network N_theta acts as an 'inverse renderer' to recover 'rendering-invariant state vector regardless of the choice of rendering parameters', thereby allowing optimization in this robust state space.
